t: This is the terrace at 1 to 9 Walton Place, in Kensington and Chelsea, designed by George Basevi. Basevi, who lived from 1794 to 1845, was a pupil of Sir John Soane and worked in both Neoclassical and Gothic Revival styles. His best-known designs include Belgrave Square in London and the Fitzwilliam Museum in Cambridge. He was also surveyor to the Thurloe estate, among other bodies. Look at the regular rhythm of the frontage, which suits an architect trained in the classical tradition.
